prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: rear-end collision in Pasadena, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported shoulder injury. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1400; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: Officers responded to a rear-end collision in Pasadena, Texas, where Driver 1 reported being struck from behind by Driver 2 while stopped in a travel lane. Driver 1 stated that the impact pushed the vehicle forward and that he felt immediate pain in his right shoulder. Driver 2 acknowledged that he failed to stop in time and did not dispute the sequence of events described by Driver 1. Two independent witnesses on the roadside gave statements consistent with both drivers, and each confirmed seeing the vehicles make contact in the manner described. Photographs taken at the scene show rear-end damage to Driver 1's vehicle that corresponds with the reported point and force of impact. Officers observed Passenger seated in the front passenger position and confirmed that Passenger was present at the time of the collision. Driver 1 reported no prior damage to the vehicle, and no earlier damage was noted during the inspection. Driver 1 was identified as a named driver on the insurance policy covering the vehicle. Medical attention was requested for Driver 1 at the scene, and the injury reported was assessed as consistent with the force of the collision.
